newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, FedEx sign express hub deal.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, FedEx sign express hub deal.

text.p: The U.S.-based Federal Express Corp signed an agreement with Taiwan on Tuesday to set up an express transhipment centre on the island, a statement issued by Taiwan's aeronautics authority said

"The Civil Aeronautics Administration and Federal Express signed an agreement on January 7 in which Federal Express agrees to set up its Asia-Pacific express transhipment centre in Taiwan's Chiang Kai-shek international airport," the statement said.
In June 1996, another U.S. firm, United Parcel Service US$400 million Asian express transshipment centre at Taipei's international airport.
The UPS hub would act as a transshipment centre for processing express parcels entering northeast and southeast Asia from other parts of the world, officials have said.
Opening of such a centre on the island would provide a boost to Taiwan's drive to establish itself as an attractive base for transnational firms' regional operations centres, officials have said.
Under the agreement with Federal Express, the administration would rent some 1,680 square metres of land to Federal Express in the international airport as its transshipment centre.

Federal Express, in return, promised that it would work closely with the Taiwan government on the airport's second cargo terminal development. In 1995, Taiwan unveiled an ambitious plan to turn the island into an Asia-Pacific operations centre for multinational firms.
"The (government's) Asia Pacific Regional Operations Centre initiative is fully supported by FedEx," Ducker said.
